subject: psychiatry
title: Antipsychotic Complications: Extrapyramidal Symptoms, Tardive Dyskinesia, and Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome

steps.title: Extrapyramidal Parkinsonism
steps.tx: **Drug-induced parkinsonism** develops within one to four weeks of starting high-potency dopamine D2 receptor antagonists like haloperidol. Blockade of striatal dopamine receptors disinhibits cholinergic interneurons, generating classical cogwheel rigidity, resting pill-rolling tremor, bradykinesia, masked facies, and a slow festinating gait.

steps.title: Akathisia Presentation
steps.tx: **Subjective motor akathisia** manifests as an agonizing sense of internal motor restlessness and somatic tension, compelling patients to pace constantly, cross and uncross legs, or shift weight while standing. Akathisia is frequently misdiagnosed as worsening psychotic agitation, leading to disastrous neuroleptic dose escalations instead of proper treatment.

steps.title: Tardive Dyskinesia Mechanism
steps.tx: **Pathophysiology of tardive dyskinesia** stems from prolonged dopamine D2 receptor blockade leading to dopamine receptor up-regulation and postsynaptic supersensitivity in the nigrostriatal pathway. Involuntary, choreoathetoid movements emerge months or years later, classically involving facial grimacing, lip smacking, jaw chewing, and repetitive fly-catcher tongue darting.

steps.tx: This face is moving without its owner's permission, lips puckering and tongue darting in the repetitive rhythm of **tardive dyskinesia**. Months or years of dopamine blockade have left striatal receptors supersensitive, so the movements arrive late and may never fully leave. Older women carry the highest risk, and anticholinergics prescribed for earlier stiffness can paradoxically worsen this later disorder. Spotting perioral movements at review matters because switching strategy early, and considering vesicular monoamine transporter inhibitors, offers more than waiting for the movements to entrench.
steps.say: Involuntary perioral and tongue movements after prolonged antipsychotics are tardive dyskinesia from receptor supersensitivity.

steps.title: Tardive Dyskinesia Management
steps.tx: **Therapeutic strategy in tardive dyskinesia** requires immediate cessation of anticholinergic medications because anticholinergics worsen involuntary choreoathetoid movements by exaggerating striatal dopaminergic predominance. Clinicians should cautiously transition the patient to clozapine and initiate vesicular monoamine transporter 2 (VMAT2) inhibitors, specifically valbenazine or deutetrabenazine, to deplete presynaptic dopamine stores.

steps.title: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
steps.tx: **Neuroleptic malignant syndrome presentation** is a rare, idiosyncratic medical emergency characterized by the classic diagnostic tetrad of severe hyperthermia exceeding 38 to 40 degrees Celsius, generalized lead-pipe muscular rigidity, profound autonomic instability with labile blood pressure, and fluctuating delirium progressing rapidly toward stupor.

left.title: NMS Clinical Features
points: Extreme hyperthermia >38C, lead-pipe generalized rigidity, labile blood pressure, diaphoresis, and severe mental obtundation

right.title: Malignant Catatonia
points: Preceding psychiatric prodrome, waxy flexibility, catatonic posturing, autonomic instability

steps.title: Laboratory Markers in NMS
steps.tx: **Laboratory markers in NMS** reveal massive elevation of serum creatine kinase, often exceeding 1,000 to 50,000 international units per liter, reflecting extensive rhabdomyolysis and muscle necrosis. Concurrent marked leukocytosis between 15,000 and 30,000 cells per microliter, metabolic acidosis, hyperkalemia, and myoglobinuria threaten acute tubular necrosis and renal failure.

steps.title: Emergency Treatment of NMS
steps.tx: **Emergency management of neuroleptic malignant syndrome** begins with instant withdrawal of all triggering antipsychotics, aggressive external physical cooling, and rapid intravenous fluid resuscitation to prevent renal cast precipitation. Intravenous dantrolene sodium directly uncouples excitation-contraction coupling in skeletal muscle, while bromocriptine or amantadine restores central dopaminergic tone.

steps.title: Depot Preparations and Cardiotoxicity
steps.tx: **Long-acting injectable antipsychotics** including fluphenazine decanoate, haloperidol decanoate, and paliperidone palmitate improve long-term therapeutic compliance in chronic schizophrenia. However, clinicians must vigilantly monitor electrocardiograms for dose-dependent QTc prolongation, especially with intravenous haloperidol, ziprasidone, and thioridazine, which can trigger lethal polymorphic ventricular tachycardia or torsades de pointes.
